name: One System CRM
author: OneSystemCRM

sections.description:
Small changes to your website should not mean waiting days for a developer.

One System CRM connects your WordPress site to the One System assistant. You type what you want, like “change our Saturday hours to 9 to 2” or “update the phone number in the footer”. The assistant finds the right spot on your Elementor page and shows you a before and after preview.

You decide how changes go live: approve each before-and-after preview in One System, ask Claude (through our connector) to make a change and confirm it there, or turn on SEO Autopilot for small SEO fixes such as page titles and image descriptions. Every change is recorded with its original and can be undone.

This plugin needs a One System account (there is a free plan). It does nothing until a site administrator connects it.

Connecting lets One System edit your site’s content (pages, posts, menus, images, SEO fields) on your behalf when you or an app you allow asks. It cannot install or change plugins, themes, users or WordPress settings. You can disconnect at any time.

What you can change

  • Text and headings on your existing pages, built with Elementor, the block editor or the classic editor
  • Titles, excerpts, content, status and featured images of your posts, pages and WooCommerce products
  • Phone numbers, emails, addresses and opening hours, everywhere at once
  • Images and links, and image titles, captions and descriptions in your media library
  • Categories and tags
  • New draft posts and pages for you to review and publish
  • Your site’s llms.txt: a short text about your business for AI assistants
  • Page SEO titles and meta descriptions
  • Your WordPress menus: add a page, rename or remove an item, put an item under another one
  • Colors and fonts of existing elements (you can switch design changes off on the One System page)

What it does not do

It edits the content you already have, and can add new posts or pages as drafts that you publish yourself. It does not design new pages or change your layout, and it can never run code, add shortcodes, edit theme or plugin files, install anything, or change your WordPress settings, users, plugins or themes. For bigger changes, you can ask our team.

Also included in your One System account

  • A simple CRM: contacts, inbox, calendar, reviews, email and SMS
  • One System booking, form, reviews and chat widgets for Elementor, with shortcodes for sites without Elementor
  • Submissions from your existing forms (Elementor Forms, Contact Form 7, WPForms, Gravity Forms, Fluent Forms) in your contacts
  • Free website health check
  • Monthly SEO and website security monitoring (paid services)

Free plan

The free plan is free forever. It includes change previews, 100 contacts, free SEO tools, a monthly security check and 30 AI credits. Paid services start with a 7 day free trial. See pricing at https://onesystemcrm.com

External services

This plugin connects to the One System service to read and edit your page content when you request a change.

  • Service: One System CRM (https://onesystemcrm.com), app at https://copilot.onesystemcrm.com

Nothing is sent before a site administrator clicks “Connect to One System” (or enters a pairing code) on the One System page in WordPress. After connecting:

  • Website changes: One System sends signed requests to this site to read your pages, posts and products and apply the changes you approve. The plugin answers with their content, titles, excerpts, links, categories and tags, the images in your media library (addresses, titles, captions, descriptions and sizes), your llms.txt text, your WordPress menus (their names and items, when you ask for a menu change), and the list of active plugins (names and versions, for Shield’s update check). For image descriptions it also sends the addresses, titles and current descriptions of the images your pages show; One System’s AI may look at those public images to suggest descriptions.
  • Form submissions: when a visitor submits a supported WordPress form, the fields they entered and the page address are sent to One System so they appear in your contacts.
  • Widgets: to show the One System widgets, the plugin asks One System for your forms, booking calendars, chat setting and the reviews you starred. Visitors’ browsers load the booking page and form from One System in a frame; a One System form is told the address of the page it is on, so its submissions show where they came from.
  • Chat widget (only after a site administrator switches the chat bubble on on the One System page, or an editor adds the One System Chat widget to a page, and only while the chat is on in your One System account): visitors’ browsers load One System’s chat script from https://copilot.onesystemcrm.com/api/chat/widget.js (the address this plugin was built for — never an address received over the network or stored in your database) with your business’s chat id. The script shows the chat bubble; a visitor’s name, email and messages go to One System only when they start a chat.
  • The One System page in WordPress: loads your recent changes from One System, and sends Undo requests to it.
  • File check (One System Shield, only after a site administrator clicks “Allow One System to check my files”): when One System runs the check (weekly or when you ask), the plugin reads your WordPress, plugin, theme and uploads files and sends One System only file names (relative to your WordPress folder) with what it found, and the username and date of any administrator added in the last week. It never sends the contents of a file. To compare files it downloads WordPress.org’s official checksums from api.wordpress.org (for WordPress itself) and downloads.wordpress.org (for plugins from WordPress.org): WordPress.org privacy policy https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/. It never changes, moves or deletes a file.
  • Telling search engines about changes (One System SEO): when your website changes through One System (for example a fix by SEO Autopilot or an article it published), One System sends the addresses of the changed pages to IndexNow (https://www.indexnow.org, used by Bing and other search engines; Microsoft privacy statement https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement). The plugin itself sends nothing to them: it only keeps a random key that One System saves on the site and shows it at /onesystem-indexnow-.txt, so the search engine can check the request came from your website.
  • After an update: the plugin tells One System its new version number and your WordPress and Elementor version numbers once, so your One System account shows the right versions. Updates themselves come from WordPress.org.

Every request between the site and One System is signed with a key that only this site and your One System account know.

  • Terms of service: https://onesystemcrm.com/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://onesystemcrm.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin from Plugins > Add New.
  2. Open One System in the WordPress admin menu (left sidebar).
  3. Click Connect to One System and sign in or create a free account at copilot.onesystemcrm.com.
  4. Open the One System app and type your first change.
sections.faq:
Can I use it with Claude or ChatGPT?

Yes, for free. Once your site is connected, find One System in Claude’s connector directory (https://claude.ai/directory/one-system), or add the connector address shown on the One System page in Claude (Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector) or ChatGPT, sign in to One System and allow it. Claude can then change your website when you ask; One System records every change with an Undo. Claude talks to One System, not to this plugin directly, and only through the same allowlisted, signed changes described below.

Do I need Elementor?

No. Pages built with Elementor (including Elementor headers and footers) are edited element by element; posts and pages built with the block editor or the classic editor are edited too — their title, excerpt, content, status and featured image. You can also use the One System booking, form and reviews shortcodes, and send your existing forms’ submissions to your One System contacts.

Will it change my site without asking?

Only in the ways you switch on. Requests in One System show a preview and go live when you click Approve. If you connect Claude, Claude asks you before it changes anything. If you turn on SEO Autopilot (part of a paid plan), it makes small SEO fixes and publishes articles by itself; you can switch it off, pause it, or choose drafts only. Every change is recorded and can be undone.

Can I undo a change?

Yes. Every change can be undone from your One System account, or from the One System page in WordPress.

Is it free?

Yes, there is a free plan forever. Paid services have a 7 day free trial.

Does it need my WordPress password?

No. When you click Connect to One System, the plugin creates a one-time code that expires after 10 minutes. You confirm it in your One System account, and the site and your account then share a secret key. Every request is signed with that key, must be less than 5 minutes old and can’t be replayed. The key is stored encrypted in your database. Changes are made as the user who connected, with content-editing permissions only (no plugins, themes, users or settings), and Disconnect on the One System page stops all access at once.

What can One System do on my site once it’s connected?

Edit content only: pages, posts and products, menus, images and their descriptions, categories and tags, SEO titles and descriptions, and the plugin’s own settings (its llms.txt text and the IndexNow key). Requests from One System act as the user who connected the site, but while such a request runs the plugin switches off every administrative capability of that user: it cannot install, activate, update, edit or delete plugins or themes, update WordPress, edit files, create, edit or delete users, change WordPress settings, import or export, or upload files other than images. WordPress’s own permission checks apply to every post it reads or changes. Disconnect on the One System page ends all access at once.

What data leaves my site?

See “External services” below.
sections.changelog:
1.8.3

  • WordPress.org review: copying a page into a new draft needs edit rights on the page it is copied from as well, and images chosen by their media-library id (to replace an image or set a featured image) or compressed into a copy must be ones the connected user may edit — the same images the media list shows.

1.8.2

  • One System forms and booking calendars show a light “Loading the form…” / “Loading the calendar…” until they have loaded, instead of an empty space.

1.8.1

  • WordPress.org review: requests from One System act as the user who connected the site, but without any administrative capability — no plugins, themes, WordPress updates, files, users, settings, import/export or unfiltered uploads; content editing stays. The plugin’s own settings (llms.txt text, IndexNow key, File check) still need that user to be an administrator in WordPress.
  • The plugin works only with the One System address it was built for: pairing with, or switching to, any other address is refused, and the chat widget script is always loaded from that address.
  • Searching for text, and the image lists, only return posts and images the connected user may edit.
  • The One System page says plainly what connecting lets One System do.

1.8.0

  • One System’s SEO Autopilot can tell Bing (IndexNow) which pages changed: One System saves a random key on your site and the plugin shows it at /onesystem-indexnow-.txt (only that address). Uninstalling removes the key.

1.7.2

  • One System is in Claude’s connector directory: the One System page links straight to it.

1.7.1

  • The One System page shows how to use your website with Claude or ChatGPT (connector address and three steps). Sites without Elementor are no longer told that only Elementor pages can be changed.

1.7.0

  • Your whole site, not only Elementor pages: posts, pages and products built with the block editor or the classic editor can be read and changed by chat — title, excerpt, content (only the visible text, or the whole content of a page that isn’t built with Elementor), status and featured image — plus image titles, captions and descriptions in the media library, categories and tags, new draft posts and pages (published only when you ask), and your site’s llms.txt (what AI assistants read about your business). Every change is previewed, approved and can be undone like before; content changes also keep WordPress revisions.

1.6.0

  • First release on WordPress.org.
  • Edit text, phone numbers, hours, images, links, SEO titles and menus by chat, with preview, approval and undo.
  • Optional design changes (colors and fonts), One System widgets for Elementor, form submissions to your contacts, and an optional read-only Shield file check.
